term: answering a contrast; stopping at the necessary
resolution: 'Answers why this rather than otherwise' has two formal senses here. ContrastRelevant takes it as a reason false at the rival world; TwoWay takes it as one reason admitted for each outcome at its own world. A reason meeting the first varies; a necessary reason cannot meet it. 'Stops at the necessary' also has two senses. ReasonClosed allows a noncontingent member, which may be a fact that is no being's existence fact; BeingStop requires a necessary being's existence fact. No inference passes from one sense to the other. Comparison keeps them as separate conjuncts, and no attributed source is read as fixing either sense.
